note: Restored wetland pools and bottomland on the Nodaway River north of St. Joseph, managed for waterfowl. MDC marks four primitive camping spots: a wooded 'Campground' on its own lane off the gravel road south of the headquarters, a lot-side spot on Squirrel Road north of the headquarters (this pin), and two lot-side spots on the gravel road along the east boundary. The campground and the Squirrel Road spot lie inside the map's Waterfowl Hunting Only Zone, where the brochure permits no other activity from October 15 to the end of the North Zone duck season; the two east spots are in the open zone. In November 2026 MDC says the Highway B bridge south of the office is being replaced and the west side must be reached from the north on Highway B. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: four map/GIS-designated primitive camping spots (pin = GIS 261, the lot-side spot on Squirrel Rd). The map-labelled 'Campground' (GIS 260, 1.5 km S, own lane) is the main camp: move the pin there. The Oct 15 - Mar 1 refuge does not cover any camping spot, but the west two (campground and pin) are inside the Waterfowl Hunting Only Zone (Oct 15 to end of duck season). Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights now manual. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION OK: area page 'Things to Do: Camping: Designated Camping Sites | Individual Campsites'; brochure (02/2025) 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map'; the map (Last Updated 6/9/2023) has four 'Primitive Camping' symbols, one of them on an MDC improved road labelled 'Campground'; GIS 27 points 260-263. Rule 140 standard; Rule 186 (waterfowl) present; no special-use-only rule, no Rule 101.

PIN / MAIN CAMP (1.48 km move proposed): stored 40.09211,-95.07872 = GIS 261, a lot-side spot at the west boundary on Squirrel Rd (33 m from lot 1317, the ADA lot; grass beside a small gravel lot). The area's clear main camp is the one the map labels 'Campground' (GIS 260, 40.07903,-95.07591): a wooded strip ~80 x 250 m south of the gravel road that runs east from Highway B just south of the headquarters, entered by its own MDC improved lane at its NE corner. Leaf-on imagery shows the gravel entrance and a glimpse of the lane under the canopy but no pads, so the pin can only be given as the GIS point, 40.07903,-95.07591 (~20 m inside the entrance). Suggest moving the pin there. Nothing else in campgrounds.json within 6 km.

CLUSTERS: GIS 262 (40.10066,-95.02352) and 263 (40.10739,-95.02324) are single lot-side spots on the gravel road along the east boundary, 4.8 and 5.0 km from the pin and 750 m apart; each is one small lot (263's is a gravel lot beside grain bins at a road junction; 262's point is in woods ~70 m from its lot). They fail the split rule's 'more than a single small lot', so no split proposed - but they are the only spots outside the waterfowl hunting zone (next flag).

SEASON CONFLICT (stored season is manual, so not written): the waterfowl closure does NOT close any camping spot outright - the map's two 'Waterfowl Refuge (Oct. 15 through Mar. 1)' hatchings (Pin Oak Pool/Rail Marsh/Ash Grove Marsh and the Sanctuary no-hunting block) are in the middle of the area, 1.5 km+ from every camping symbol. BUT the map's diagonal 'Waterfowl Hunting Only Zone (Oct. 15 to end of North Zone Duck Season)' hatching covers the whole west block, including the 'Campground' parcel and the Squirrel Rd lot; the brochure says of those zones 'No other activities are permitted in these zones, including scouting for future hunts, at any time from Oct. 15 through the end of the North Zone Duck Season.' Read literally, the campground and the pin spot are closed to camping from Oct 15 to the end of duck season (about the end of December), and the east spots (open zone) are not. The stored season note ('Portions of the area are closed to protect waterfowl, October 15 through March 1.') understates this for the main camp. Suggested by hand: season note 'The campground and the Squirrel Road spot are inside the Waterfowl Hunting Only Zone: no other use from October 15 to the end of the North Zone duck season. The two east-side spots stay open.' I could not confirm with MDC whether duck hunters with a daily permit camp there in season.

ACCESS / CURRENT NOTICE: area page: 'If you are planning to travel to the west side of the Nodaway Valley Conservation Area be aware that the Highway B bridge south of the office is being replaced. To access the Nodaway Valley HQ or the west side of the area you must come in from the north on Highway B.' Undated on the page; recorded in the note, not as a status (the campsites are not closed by it). Roads are paved Highway B and gravel county roads; no ford or 4WD wording.
WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept. The pin spot looks over fields; the campground is in woods ~400 m from the nearest pool; the Nodaway River is 2 km+ from the west spots.
HORSES: brochure 'Bicycles and horses allowed on public roadways.' No horse camp.

PHONE: page '(660) 626-1797' matches stored. The 02/2025 brochure prints 'Nodaway Valley CA (660) 446-3371 or St. Joseph Regional Office (816) 271-3100' - the area office number differs from the page's; the page is the standard checked here.
FACILITIES: the map's privy symbols are at the pools' lots, none at a camping spot (not written).
